lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Hey. Come on in, grab a chair.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: I'm good, thanks. So I read the note you posted last night. About versioning.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Yeah, I figured that's what we'd talk about.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Okay. So. I'm just gonna say it. Any change needs both sides to approve? That worries me. A lot.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Okay. Tell me what you're picturing.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: I'm picturing us wanting to ship something on a Tuesday, and it sits in Montague's inbox for three weeks because Romeo's on vacation. We move fast here. And now we've handed someone else a brake pedal.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: That's fair. That's a real thing that happens. But I think the rule's a lot narrower than it sounded in the note. That's on me, I wrote it fast.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Narrower how?

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: It only covers the inspection record. The shared format. So, site ID, inspector, photos, findings, signed at. The stuff that actually crosses the bridge.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Right, but that's the, I mean, that's the core of the app.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: It's the core of what we send them. It's not the core of Balcony. How we store things on the device, the photo cache, the screens, the offline stuff, all of that is ours. Nobody at Montague gets a vote on any of it. They don't even see it.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: So if I want to restructure the local database...

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Go for it. Doesn't touch the rule. Only if you change what goes out in the record. And honestly, it cuts both ways. Montague owns the routing envelope. If they change that, they need us to sign off. So they can't break us either.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Huh. Okay. I hadn't really thought about it from that side.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: That's the part I like. It protects us too, especially with Ducal in the middle.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Yeah. Okay. But I still want a clock on it. Because, the vacation thing, that's not hypothetical.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Totally agree. What feels right? A week?

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: A week's too long. Two days. Forty-eight hours. If the other side hasn't said anything in forty-eight hours, it's, uh, it's not a veto. You can't block by just going quiet.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Forty-eight hour review window. I like that. And it goes both ways, same rule for them.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Same rule for them, sure. That's only fair. Right. Neither side blocks the other. That's what I care about.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Good. I'll run it by Romeo today and write it into the spec.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Cool. And, um, one more thing.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: The airplane-mode thing. I said yesterday I'd believe the queue if it survives a week of airplane mode. I should probably be the one to actually test that, instead of just, you know, saying it in standup.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Ha. Are you volunteering?

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: I'm volunteering. I'll write the airplane-mode test. Device offline, pile of inspections, bring it back, make sure everything lands in order. I'll fake the week with the clock.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Please fake the week. I need you back before Friday.

lines.speaker: tybalt_capulet
lines.text: Yeah, yeah. I'll have it before go or no-go. And I'm not gonna go easy on it. Okay. Thanks. Sorry for coming in hot.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: You didn't. Well, a little. It's fine. Go write your test.
